messages:
alex: New account ready in us-west2 for a GPU fleet (P40 -> initial test, then scale to A100s). Need guidance on subnet sizing and NAT capacity. We're seeing pod failures when we try to spin up ~60 nodes in a single AZ.

natalie: Do you have the node pool CIDR right now? sounds like classic /24 exhaustion if everything is in one subnet.

alex: Current VPC: 10.40.0.0/16. Worker subnet is 10.40.1.0/24 for us-west2-a. We used /24 by default — I think we need /22 or split across AZs.

raj: If you want 60+ GPU nodes + autoscaling, /24 won't cut it. Each node needs IPs for kubelet, pod IPs, NAT mappings etc. For GKE with VPC-native, pods also consume address space. I'd recommend at least /22 per AZ or use secondary ranges.

yvonne: Also check SNAT port allocation on Cloud NAT. When we ran a batch of 1000 jobs last month we hit ephemeral port exhaustion because each pod opened multiple outbound connections per model shard download.

alex: Good call. We're seeing many 'connection refused' / timeout errors in logs when provisioning models. infra-bot: "Detected 502s from model downlaods — suspect egress throttling."

natalie: Two parallel asks for cloud support: 1) Increase quota for static external IPs for NAT gateways in us-west2 to 6 (current 1). 2) Increase Cloud NAT ephemeral port pool. Message the provider with flows/traffic numbers.

alex: Drafted a ticket to cloud-support referencing current project, region, and expected scale. Ticket details: "Need additional external IPs for per-AZ NAT gateways and larger ephemeral port pool for high-concurrency model pull during scale-up (expected concurrent ephemeral ports ~120k)."

cloud-support: Thanks, we've created case CS-USW2-2049. Provider asked for peak concurrent connection estimate and time window. Can you paste the kube-scheduler scale patterns?

raj: We're doing rolling scale from 10 -> 150 nodes over ~5 minutes for a ramp test. Each node when starting pulls model shards from S3 and makes ~60 concurrent connections during initialization. Estimated peak concurrent TCP sockets: 150 nodes * 60 = 9000 active from nodes, but each can spawn short-lived connections to many third-party services, multiplier ~8 -> 72k.

alex: Also we need new subnets per AZ: prefer /22 (1022 usable IPs) for us-west2-a/b/c. Can the cloud account get approval to create 3 x /22s under 10.40.0.0/16?

cloud-support: Provider asks if you can use alias IP ranges/secondary ranges instead of enlarging primary subnet. They also flagged that expanding existing subnet from /24 -> /22 might require downtime.

natalie: We can't take downtime. Suggest creating new secondary ranges and migrating nodepools with rolling upgrades. Also add explicit route propagation rules: ensure Private Google Access and VPC flow logs remain enabled.

alex: Terraform snippet I'm planning to apply for the new secondary ranges:
```hcl
resource "google_compute_subnetwork" "workers_usw2a" {
  name          = "workers-usw2a"
  ip_cidr_range = "10.40.4.0/22"
  region        = "us-west2"
  network       = "projects/prod-vpc/global/networks/main"
}
```

yvonne: Also consider using per-node NAT gateways with fewer public IPs but better SNAT distribution, costs are higher though. Quick back-of-envelope: extra NAT gateway (per AZ) ~ $0.04/hr + 0.01/GB egress, but reduces connection churn and port exhaustion.

raj: Another option: use Cloud NAT with multiple NAT IPs per NAT gateway to increase ephemeral port space; provider can increase the ephemeral port quota by allocating more NAT IP addresses. Request them to allow 12 NAT IPs per gateway.

cloud-support: We've escalated: provider will authorize up to 12 NAT IPs per gateway for your project in us-west2, pending security review. Estimated action time: 48-72 hours. Case CS-USW2-2049.

alex: Great. Any notes on inter-VPC peering? We'll peer dev/prod for model registry access and want to avoid asymmetric routing.

natalie: Use private service connect or VPC peering with managed routes. For cross-project peering, ensure you don't overlap secondary ranges. Also enable route export/import correctly; prefer a hub-and-spoke via Shared VPC to centralize NAT.

alex: One more cost question — if we provision 3 NAT gateways (one per AZ) vs 1 central NAT, what's the expected monthly delta? yvonne: Rough estimate: 3x NAT gateways -> +$65/mo + extra static IPs fees (~$3/ip/mo), but reduces failed model pulls and emergency incidents. Cheaper central NAT might save $30/mo but risk more retries and longer scale-up times.

infra-bot: "Applied terraform plan to create secondary ranges in staging cluster for test — no downtime expected."

alex: OK I'll hold off on changing primary subnet. Plan: 1) Add secondary /22 ranges in each AZ, 2) request provider increase NAT IPs to 12/gateway (case open), 3) create per-AZ NAT gateways once provider confirms static IP quota, 4) run scale test to validate ephemeral ports.

natalie: Sounds good. Tag me when the cloud-support case moves to 'approved'. :thumbsup:

cloud-support: Update CS-USW2-2049 -> approved for additional static IPs (6) and increased ephemeral ports via NAT IPs. Please attach your maintenance window for provider to apply changes.

alex: Attaching maintenance window: 2026-03-21 02:00-04:00 UTC. Please proceed.

raj: After this completes, let's add automated alerts to the observability dashboard for SNAT port usage and model pull failure rates.

yvonne: I'll add a Grafana panel and set a threshold alert at 70% port utilization.

alex: Thanks everyone — will follow up with results from the scale run.
